newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland's Alho sees no obstacle to markka ERM link.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Alho sees no obstacle to markka ERM link.

text.p: Finnish second Finance Minister Arja Alho said on Monday in a statement there were no obstacles from Finland's point of view to link the markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

"From Finland's point of view there are no obstacles to fix the currency to the ERM system," Alho said in a statement following a newspaper interview, which quoted her as saying she thought Finland should not rush into ERM.
The effectiveness of the ERM system was determined by big European economies and their ability to keep their currencies stable, she said.
"That is why we in Finland, too, must monitor the developments of the economies in the ERM system instead of constantly thinking about the value of the markka," she said.
"There is no reason for Finland to fear ERM or EMU. A small economy has more to gain than to lose in EMU," she added.
Finnish local newspaper Karjalainen on Sunday reported that Alho saw reasons to hold off on a decision on ERM, citing worrying signals from other ERM countries.
However, she also said the Finnish economy was so stable that Finland would not have any "terribly big problem" in linking the markka tomorrow or within months.
